chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'The bearers of the Throne — and the Throne is Knowledge — are eight: four from us and four from whoever God wills.'

key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Throne (al-'Arsh) — in Shia cosmology often identified with the totality of divine knowledge and authority
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: Knowledge ('ilm) — the divine knowledge that the Imams possess and transmit
key_terms.حَمَلَةُ الْعَرْشِ: Bearers of the Throne — angelic or cosmic figures who sustain the divine Throne
key_terms.مِنَّا: From us — a phrase used by the Imam to include himself and the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the bearers of the Throne (hamalat al-'arsh) in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) discloses an esoteric teaching about the cosmic Throne (al-'Arsh): it is eight in number and its reality is Knowledge itself. Four of the eight bearers are from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, and four others are appointed by divine will. This hadith belongs to the theological tradition in al-Kafi concerning the metaphysical nature of the Throne and the special role of the Imams as custodians of divine knowledge.
